Jinlong Lu is a Principal Investigator at Tsinghua University School of Medicine. His research aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms that govern aging and longevity by combining comparative proteomics and transcriptomics across mammalian species to identify conserved hallmarks and regulatory networks associated with lifespan control.
Building on these insights, he investigates rejuvenation strategies such as partial cellular reprogramming. He discovered that mesenchymal drift is a prevalent hallmark of aging and represents a promising target for rejuvenation interventions — work that also provides critical insights for dissecting rejuvenation from pluripotency, advancing safer somatic cell reprogramming-based approaches to rejuvenation.
He was previously a Senior Scientist at Altos Labs (2022–2025, reporting to Dr. Juan Carlos Izpisua Belmonte), where he works on projects on partial reprogramming and aging intervention; a Postdoctoral Researcher at the University of Rochester (2021–2022, Gorbunova & Seluanov Lab) studying comparative biology of aging; and a Postdoctoral Researcher at Tsinghua University (2019–2020, Dr. Xiaohua Shen’s lab) working on 3D genome organization and chromatin regulation. His early PhD work at Tsinghua focused on repetitive elements in genome organization and function.
